newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Nov 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Nov 15.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Bangkok Post survey shows Chavalit Yongchaiyudh will suffer a big loss in the capital. Widspread disapproval for the leader of the New Aspiration Party (NAP) will give the Democrats a landslide win in Bangkok, according to a Bangkok Post-Ramkhamhaeng poll. The survey said the Democrats will sweep 29 of Bangkok's 37 seats in the November 17 election, Palang Dharma will come in a distant second followed by Prachakorn Thai, Chart Pattana and Muan Chon. The poll, conducted for the second time to test the popularity of parties contesting Bangkok, shows voters remain firm in their support of the Democrats. (BANGKOK POST) - Democrats, NAP predict tight race despite survey. Both the Democrat and New Aspiration Parties shrugged off the latest and largest opinion poll which predicted a clear election victory for Democrat leader Chuan Leekpai, as the significance of smaller parties grew in the home stretch of the race for premiership. Both parties' final strategies are based on their own predictions of a neck-and-neck contest. This means election battles in crucial, decisive areas such as the four southern most provinces will be fierce. (THE NATION)

- Car giants to catch Clinton on brief visit. U.S. automakers General Motors and Ford have invited President Bill Clinton to preside over two grand ceremonies to bolster their large investment projects, worth a combined Bt27.35 billion, during the American president's visit to Thailand on Nov 25-26, according to company and government officials. (THE NATION).

- The new government will have five urgent tasks to revive the Thai economy, according to Board of Investment Secretary-General Staporn Kavitanond. The task are: restoring confidence among investors; improving the competitiveness of Thai products; decentralisation; efficient measures to increase exports and clearer strategies to increase Thai investment abroad. (BANGKOK POST)

- Advance Info Service Plc will be penalised for misleading advertising for its GSM mobile phones. The Consumer Protection Board found a subscriber who bought a GSM mobile phone last year on the understanding the digital network would expand nationwide soon. But the company has yet to expand the network. (BANGKOK POST)
